# ArchiGen AI

> An evidence-led editorial publication for architects, archviz artists, and design-forward studios working out where AI fits into practice, from concept sketch to client-ready render. Articles compare tools and workflows, cite their sources, and state what kind of evidence stands behind each claim. No sponsored placements.

ArchiGen AI is owned and operated by Vista Studios and published by Quincy, ArchiGen's human owner and publisher, who reviews and approves every piece published here. Articles are bylined Nora Sinclair. Nora Sinclair is ArchiGen's AI editorial persona, not a human architect or practitioner; every piece published under Nora's name is reviewed and approved by Quincy, who is accountable for its editorial decisions and corrections.

Evidence standard: ArchiGen articles are editorial analysis based on cited vendor documentation, published comparisons and community reports. Hands-on testing is claimed only where an article documents the test (tool and version, test date, inputs, settings, outputs). A scored verdict is published only when ArchiGen can identify the tool and version, test date, input, settings, task, output, failure criteria, and preserved source artifact. Figures are labeled as actual tested-tool output, vendor or third-party media, or editorial illustration. Vista-owned products are ineligible for scores, rankings, or awards.

## Editorial standards

- [How to Read AI Rendering Tool Rankings](https://archigenai.com/rankings-claims-audits.html): Hub page for every ArchiGen audit of AI rendering rankings, roundups and vendor claims, grouped by the question each answers.
- [Masthead](https://archigenai.com/masthead.html): Ownership (Vista Studios), human publisher accountability, the Nora Sinclair AI persona disclosure, the testing and ratings policy, and the corrections policy.
- [About](https://archigenai.com/about.html): What ArchiGen covers, what it does not do, and how reviews qualify for a scored verdict.

## Core guides

- [An Honest Guide to AI Rendering in Architecture](https://archigenai.com/honest-guide-ai-rendering-architecture.html): What AI rendering does and does not do for architects, with tool-by-tool assessments of Midjourney, FLUX, ComfyUI and Leonardo and when not to use AI rendering at all.
- [The Honest Guide to AI Rendering in 2026](https://archigenai.com/honest-guide-ai-rendering.html): What AI rendering can and can't do for practices today, five common adoption mistakes, and how to evaluate a tool before buying a seat.
- [Best AI Tools for Architectural Visualization 2026](https://archigenai.com/best-ai-tools-architectural-visualization-2026.html): A ranked comparison of AI visualization tools including Midjourney, Chaos Veras and Stable Diffusion, with the evaluation criteria stated on the page.
- [Prompt Engineering for Architectural Exteriors](https://archigenai.com/prompt-engineering-architectural-exteriors.html): A seven-parameter framework for writing prompts that produce consistent exterior renders.
- [What does AI build when architects are in charge?](https://archigenai.com/architects-in-charge.html): An essay on what AI produces when architects direct the tools rather than follow them, and on human authorship in generative design.

## Evaluating AI render tools

- [The Fair AI Render Benchmark for Architects](https://archigenai.com/ai-render-tool-benchmark-protocol-architects-2026.html): A repeatable protocol for comparing Veras, Rendair AI, Archsynth, Gendo, D5, Enscape and similar tools without mixing incompatible jobs.
- [Build an Evidence Ladder for AI Render Tool Recommendations](https://archigenai.com/ai-render-recommendation-evidence-ladder-architects-2026.html): Separating product claims, comparison summaries, community reports and project-tested facts.
- [The Geometry-Hallucination QA Checklist](https://archigenai.com/ai-render-geometry-hallucination-qa-checklist-architects-2026.html): Failure modes AI renderers introduce and a review routine before a render reaches the client.
- [Cost Per Usable Image](https://archigenai.com/ai-render-cost-per-usable-image-architects-2026.html): Why price per generation understates cost, and how to measure your own keeper rate before committing to a plan.
- [The 2026 "Best AI Tools for Architects" Listicles, Audited](https://archigenai.com/best-ai-tools-architects-listicles-audited-2026.html): A reading of the 2026 best-tools listicles and a filter for which recurring tools earn their place.

## Workflows

- [Blender + ComfyUI: A Tested Architectural Rendering Workflow](https://archigenai.com/blender-comfyui-architectural-rendering-workflow-test.html): A documented local test (RTX 3090, Blender 5.2.0 LTS, ComfyUI 0.37.0) with settings, approved interior renders, AI mistakes and masking steps.
- [ComfyUI Sketch-to-Photoreal for Architecture](https://archigenai.com/comfyui-sketch-to-photoreal-architecture.html): A ComfyUI workflow for turning hand sketches into renders while holding the building's geometry.
- [ComfyUI Advanced: Exterior Workflows](https://archigenai.com/comfyui-advanced-tutorial.html): Depth ControlNet, material passes, site-context inpainting and lighting control for exterior renders.
- [Veras Inside Revit in 2026](https://archigenai.com/veras-revit-bim-render-workflow-2026.html): The BIM-native Veras workflow in Revit compared with exporting to SketchUp.
- [Nano Banana 2 vs GPT Image 2 for Floor Plans](https://archigenai.com/gpt-image-2-vs-nano-banana-2-floor-plan-comparison.html): Nano Banana 2 and GPT Image 2 compared for rendering residential floor plans.
- [AI Rendering on a Mac](https://archigenai.com/ai-rendering-on-a-mac-architects-2026.html): What runs natively on Apple Silicon, what needs a workaround, and where cloud tools fill the gap.
- [AI Rendering for Small Firms, Budget Tiers](https://archigenai.com/ai-rendering-small-firms-budget-tiers.html): Building an AI rendering stack at free, $50/month, $200/month and studio budgets.
- [Who Owns Your AI Render, and Can You Bill For It?](https://archigenai.com/who-owns-ai-render-commercial-license-architects-2026.html): Model licences versus rights in generated images, for architects putting renders on fee proposals.
